findings.title: Good and evil as paired directions of one accountable deed
findings.claim: The focus act is the evil-directed counterpart of the good-directed act immediately before it, so the pericope presents one accountable action frame with opposite moral directions.
findings.mechanism: The 99:7 clause repeats the focus action, measure, particle, and seeing frame while changing the value term to good; 99:8 changes that term to evil, making the focus a paired negative member rather than an isolated warning.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the final clause as the second side of a deliberately repeated rule: the same personal encounter reaches both moral directions at the same atom-scale.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains a person's seeing the evil they did. The paired relation does not erase the distinction between good and evil or assert that the two outcomes are identical.

epistemic.reason: The counterpart is an exact supplied 99:7-99:8 connection and the cited focus branches are lexically supplied; the interpretive change is the bounded relation between them.
